# ashlr-plugin agent reference

> Install with npm, call the CLI with --json, and register the ashlr-mcp server.

This file is the copy-paste reference for agents. The rendered documentation corpus, which includes every public doc page, is https://plugin.ashlr.ai/llms-full.txt. The short index is https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-plugin/blob/main/llms.txt and https://plugin.ashlr.ai/llms.txt.

Local tools need no account. Telemetry is off unless `ASHLR_TELEMETRY=on`. Requires Bun 1.3 or newer.

## Install

```bash
npm install -g ashlr-plugin
ashlr-plugin --ashlr-handshake
ashlr-plugin version
ashlr-plugin tools --json
ashlr-plugin manifest --json
ashlr-plugin stats --json
ashlr-plugin doctor --json
ashlr-plugin codex-doctor --json
ashlr-plugin codex-install --dry-run --json
```

The README pins the current npm release. `npm install -g ashlr-plugin` installs the latest. `--ashlr-handshake` is answered by the `ashlr-plugin` program and prints one JSON object whose `kind` is `ashlr.handshake`.

Every subcommand that takes `--json` prints one JSON object whose first key is `schema`, named `ashlr-plugin.<command>.v1` (for example `ashlr-plugin.tools.v1`). Check it before reading the rest. Fields are only added within `v1`; a breaking change gets `v2`. A result that is not an object, such as a missing stats slice, prints as `{ "schema", "value": null }`.

`tools --json` prints `{ "schema", "count", "tools": [{ "name", "description" }] }`. `stats --json` prints the ledger at `~/.ashlr/stats.json`. An empty ledger looks like this:

```json
{
  "schema": "ashlr-plugin.stats.v1",
  "schemaVersion": 2,
  "sessions": {},
  "lifetime": {
    "calls": 0,
    "tokensSaved": 0,
    "rawTotal": 0,
    "byTool": {},
    "byDay": {}
  }
}
```

From a checkout of this repo, CLI subcommands also run as `bun run scripts/cli.ts <subcommand>`. Do not pass `--ashlr-handshake` to `cli.ts`. That flag is handled by `scripts/ashlr-plugin.mjs`.

`manifest --json` lists every shipped skill and slash command: `{ "schema", "schemaVersion": 1, "name", "version", "commands": [{ "name", "description", "path" }], "skills": [{ "name", "description", "path" }] }`. Paths are relative to the installed package. Discovery does not run the instructions. Empty inventories return empty arrays.

`doctor --json` compares installed skills, commands and hooks against the CLI's shipped file manifest: `{ "schema", "schemaVersion": 1, "ok", "root", "checked", "issues": [{ "path", "status", "fix" }] }`. Status is `missing`, `stale` (changed contents), or `unreadable`. Use `doctor` for plain-word fixes or add `--root <plugin-folder>` to check a host's cached copy. Offline and read-only; exits 0 when clean, 1 for issues. `codex-doctor` checks Codex configuration separately.

## CLI reference

Every subcommand. `ashlr-plugin help` prints the same list.

```bash
ashlr-plugin stats --json [--session <id>] [--since <YYYY-MM-DD>] [--tool <name>]
ashlr-plugin tools [--json]
ashlr-plugin manifest [--json]
ashlr-plugin mcp
ashlr-plugin codex-start [--json]
ashlr-plugin codex-resume [--json]
ashlr-plugin codex-end [--json]
ashlr-plugin codex-doctor [--json]
ashlr-plugin doctor [--json] [--root <plugin-folder>]
ashlr-plugin codex-install --dry-run [--json]
ashlr-plugin genome-refresh [--json] [--full] [--dry-run] [--quiet] [--debounce <ms>]
ashlr-plugin selftest [--json] [--only <id|command,...>] [--keep-tmp] [--timeout-ms <n>]
ashlr-plugin recut-plan --base <ref> [--head <ref>]
ashlr-plugin version
```

- `stats` requires `--json` and returns one slice at a time: `--session` wins over `--tool`, which wins over `--since`. `--since` returns `{ "schema", "daily": { "<date>": ... } }` from `lifetime.byDay`.
- `mcp` starts the stdio MCP router; `ashlr-mcp` is the same server as a standalone bin.
- `codex-start`, `codex-resume` and `codex-end` print session guidance only; no hooks run.
- `codex-install` supports `--dry-run` only and writes nothing.
- `genome-refresh` processes pending changed paths. `--full` rebuilds affected genomes, `--dry-run` previews, `--quiet` (implied by `--json`) silences worker messages, and `--debounce` defaults to 0.
- `selftest` runs every command's entry point against a throwaway fixture repo. Run `ashlr-plugin selftest --help` for its options.
- `recut-plan` always prints JSON: a read-only merge diagnosis of local Git refs. `--head` defaults to `HEAD`. It exits 0 for a clean or conflicting diagnosis and 2 when refs or a common ancestor are unavailable.
- `version` prints plain text: `ashlr-plugin` followed by the version.

Claude Code plugin (hooks, slash commands, status line). This does not install the global npm bin:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://plugin.ashlr.ai/install.sh | bash
```

Inside Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add ashlrai/ashlr-plugin
/plugin install ashlr@ashlr-marketplace
/reload-plugins
```

Codex plugin:

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add ashlrai/ashlr-plugin
codex plugin add ashlr@ashlr-marketplace
ashlr-plugin codex-doctor --json
```

Windows PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ashlrai/ashlr-plugin/main/docs/install.ps1 | iex
```

## MCP server

`ashlr-mcp` must be on PATH (`npm install -g ashlr-plugin`). Paste one snippet. Do not edit a path.

Claude Code, `.mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ashlr": {
      "command": "ashlr-mcp",
      "args": [],
      "env": {
        "ASHLR_MCP_HOST": "claude-code"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Cursor, `.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ashlr": {
      "command": "ashlr-mcp",
      "args": [],
      "env": {
        "ASHLR_MCP_HOST": "cursor"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Codex, `~/.codex/config.toml`. Same server the dry-run plans:

```toml
[mcp_servers.ashlr]
command = "ashlr-mcp"
args = []
cwd = "."
env = { ASHLR_MCP_HOST = "codex-cli", ASHLR_CODEX_HOOK_MODE = "nudge" }
```

## Tool calls

`ashlr__read` and `ashlr__grep` do not modify files. Call them through the connected MCP server.
`ashlr__grep` requires ripgrep (`rg`) on PATH. By default, large supported JavaScript and TypeScript reads can return an AST skeleton; use `mode: "snip"` for the head-and-tail path, which may still use LLM summarization. `bypassSummary: true` returns full file content without AST or LLM summarization, even after a cached compact read. Read output can include line numbers and accounting notes.

```json
{ "name": "ashlr__read", "arguments": { "path": "README.md" } }
```

For selected lines without summarization, pass a 1-based inclusive range. Omit `endLine` for up to 200 lines from `startLine`, capped at the file end. `endLine` requires `startLine`.

```json
{ "name": "ashlr__read", "arguments": { "path": "README.md", "startLine": 1, "endLine": 20 } }
```

```json
{ "name": "ashlr__grep", "arguments": { "pattern": "registerTool", "cwd": "servers" } }
```

```json
{ "name": "ashlr__savings", "arguments": {} }
```

`ashlr__edit` writes a file. Required arguments are `path`, `search`, and `replace`. Use it only when you mean to change that file.

## Savings

Published per-call figures, not a whole session, from the 2026-10-17 reference run: reads about 75% smaller, greps about 27% smaller. Per-repo means on that run: about 60% on vercel/ai, about 63% on pandas, about 55% on tokio. Reproduce with:

```bash
bun run scripts/run-benchmark.ts --compare
```

Methodology: https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-plugin/blob/main/docs/benchmarks.md

## Ecosystem

ashlr-plugin is the efficiency layer of the Ashlr ecosystem. Phantom and its sibling repos form an autonomous, code-first, agent-native software factory: agents do the engineering and maintain each repo, the human sits as a passive board member, and the goal is open source RSI (recursive self-improvement).

- Phantom: the engineering agent workbench (`phm` CLI, JSON interface, MCP gateway). https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom
- Phantom Secrets: agents use API keys through `phm_` placeholders swapped back at a local proxy. https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom-secrets
- Locus: identity pinning for CLI commands, MCP tools and agent sessions. https://github.com/ashlrai/locus
- Lexicon: personal voice lexicon for speech-to-text names. https://github.com/ashlrai/lexicon
- Ashlr Stack: service setup from the terminal or an agent. https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-stack
- Ashlr MD: desktop Markdown app with on-device AI. https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md

`ashlr-plugin --ashlr-handshake` prints capabilities and health as JSON, so Phantom and other agents can discover the plugin without parsing `--help`. Contract: https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-plugin/blob/main/docs/ashlr-handshake.md

To run the plugin inside the Phantom Secrets boundary, start the host with `phantom exec -- claude` or `phantom exec -- codex`; the plugin passes the `phm_` placeholder and base URL through unchanged. Details: https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-plugin/blob/main/docs/PHANTOM-USAGE.md

Agents work on this repository directly: they branch, commit, open pull requests and merge on green under https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-plugin/blob/main/AGENTS.md. From a checkout:

```bash
bun install
bunx tsc --noEmit
bun test __tests__/readme-links.test.ts __tests__/readme-commands-samples.test.ts __tests__/agent-front-door.test.ts
```

Then scan the diff for secrets, open a PR, and arm auto-merge. `CI Gate` (`fast checks` plus `Secret-shape scan`) is the single required check, and the PR lands through the merge queue once it is green. A maintainer arms auto-merge for fork PRs. Full path: https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-plugin/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#from-branch-to-main

```bash
git diff origin/main...HEAD | perl .github/tests/secret-shape/scrub.pl --check --allow-fixtures
gh pr merge --auto
```

Without write access, work from a fork. `gh repo fork --clone` sets `origin` to your fork and `upstream` to ashlrai/ashlr-plugin. Push the branch to your fork and open the PR against upstream `main`. `CI Gate` runs the same way, and a maintainer or fleet agent arms auto-merge. GitHub can hold workflow runs from a first-time contributor until a maintainer approves them. Full path, with a prompt to hand your agent: https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-plugin/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contribute-from-a-fork-with-your-own-agent

```bash
gh repo fork ashlrai/ashlr-plugin --clone && cd ashlr-plugin && bun install
git switch -c fix/<topic>
# make the change and run the checks above
git push -u origin fix/<topic>
gh pr create --repo ashlrai/ashlr-plugin --base main --head <your-github-user>:fix/<topic> --fill
```
